title: You wouldn’t expect a traitor to become a testimony.
paragraphs: You wouldn’t expect a traitor to become a testimony.
That’s how the story begins—wrong, uncomfortable, almost offensive if you don’t slow down and really see it.
“But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them…” (Joshua 2:4)
That word carries weight. Intent. Risk. A decision that couldn’t be undone.
Jericho was her home. Her people. Her protection. Everything familiar. And in one moment, Rahab chose against all of it.
Because something inside her had already shifted long before those spies knocked on her door.
“For we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you… and what you did to Sihon and Og… whom you devoted to destruction.” (Joshua 2:10)
She knew exactly who Israel’s God was.
“And as soon as we heard it, our hearts melted… for the Lord your God, He is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath.” (Joshua 2:11)
While everyone else in Jericho heard the same stories and chose denial, Rahab heard—and believed.
That’s the dividing line most people don’t realize.
You’ve heard enough truth about God to know this isn’t just religion.
That quiet moment when everything in you knew—this is real.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Belief that costs you nothing isn’t belief. It’s observation.
Rahab didn’t just believe internally. She acted externally.
When the king’s men came asking, she stood in the gap and lied to protect the spies:
“Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from…” (Joshua 2:4)
She chose God over her people before she ever met Him personally.
That’s the part that unsettles you.
Because you’ve been trying to hold both.
And once you see it, you realize this wasn’t betrayal for betrayal’s sake.
She abandoned a life that Scripture openly identifies as broken—she was a prostitute in a pagan city—and aligned herself with a holy God she had only heard about.
This is where the tension tightens.
Because if you’re honest, you’ve been waiting for more evidence before surrendering.
Rahab had less than you—and moved faster.
She risked her life on what she knew about God.
You hesitate with everything you’ve been given.
And here’s where it breaks open—
Her betrayal didn’t lead to destruction.
“And Joshua saved Rahab the prostitute alive… because she hid the messengers…” (Joshua 6:25)
While Jericho burned, she stood untouched.
While walls fell, she remained standing.
And it goes deeper than survival.
She becomes part of God’s story.
She is listed in the lineage of Jesus Christ (Matthew 1:5).
Becomes part of the bloodline of the Savior.
So now you’re left with something you can’t ignore.
Every compromise is a quiet agreement.
Do you stay where it’s safe—with what’s familiar, even if it’s against God?
Or do you cross the line like Rahab did… and risk everything to align with truth?
Because one path leads to collapse.
If you know you’ve been holding onto both sides, say it plainly—no performance, no hiding.
If you feel that pull to turn, don’t silence it.
And if you’ve been watching from a distance, it’s time to step closer.
There’s more depth waiting—truth that corrects, exposes, and rebuilds you the right way.
Walk it with others who aren’t pretending anymore.
And when it does… you’ll remember Rahab.
